subject: Copywriting
title: The Landing Page as Sales Letter
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Landing Page as Sales Letter.

hook.text: Every long-form landing page is a sales letter with better fonts.

buildup.text: The transition from mail to web happened in the early 2000s.

discovery.text: ClickFunnels, built by Russell Brunson, turned the sales letter into a multi-step funnel.

twist.text: Short landing pages generally underperform long ones for high-priced products.

climax.text: Digital added video, animations, and interactive elements.

punchline.text: New medium, same letter. Landing pages are sales letters with links.

quiz.question: Who built ClickFunnels, turning the sales letter into a digital funnel?

details.summary: The modern landing page is a sales letter reformatted for screens. Long-form landing pages follow the exact same structure — headline, lead, proof, offer, close — as direct mail letters that generated millions. The medium changed; the psychology didn't.
details.whyItMatters: Understanding that landing pages are digital sales letters connects modern marketers to a century of proven copywriting wisdom. The tactical details change, but the persuasion principles are identical.
takeaways: Landing pages follow the same headline-lead-body-close structure as sales letters
Long-form landing pages consistently outperform short ones for high-ticket products
Visual hierarchy replaced physical letter layout as the design challenge

faq.question: Why do long landing pages still work?
faq.answer: Because high-consideration purchases require high-information decisions. A $2,000 course needs more persuasion than a $10 book. Long pages give prospects all the information, proof, and reassurance they need without leaving the page to research elsewhere.

faq.question: What's different about web sales letters versus mail?
faq.answer: Web letters can include video, interactive elements, and real-time social proof. Readers can scroll at their own pace and click to buy instantly. But the core challenge is identical: earn attention, build desire, prove claims, overcome objections, and ask for the sale.
